items.title: Bounty scanner: a CI job that searches GitHub daily for open issues with a bounty label or `/bounty $` comment, reads amount, language, repo activity, licence and contribution rules, excludes security-testing repositories and vulnerability reports, ranks by amount × fit ÷ age, writes docs/bounties/BOARD.md and files a queue item for the top three
items.why: RESEARCH §2: 553 open labelled bounties today and no routine reads them; the GitHub API is reachable from every sandbox and the runner (GITHUB_TOKEN suffices for search). Fit = TypeScript/JavaScript/Python/Rust, tests present, a CONTRIBUTING that does not forbid AI-assisted work. Built 2026-10-11 (interactive): scripts/bounty-scanner.ts + .github/workflows/bounty-board.yml (05:17 daily); first board read 498 issues, kept 56 with an amount, filed three.
items.proof: BOARD.md refreshed daily with ranked bounties; three queue items filed from it

items.title: First bounty: take the scanner's top-ranked issue, fork, fix with tests in the project's conventions, open the PR with `/claim #<issue>` and a plain note on how it was built, then track it to merge
items.why: The posted amount is the proof of demand; a merged PR is the whole sale. Needs PR_TOKEN (action 021) to push the fork from CI and the board sign-in (action 022) so the claim resolves to the owner's account. Unblocked 2026-10-11: PR_TOKEN present and the owner signed in to the board with their GitHub account. Dropped 2026-10-18 (review W42): no free funded code row appeared on seven daily boards (10-11..10-17); the line is killed and the queue finished. If the exchange reopens the queue on its trigger, this is the first item again.
items.proof: PR merged and the bounty paid (revenue row in docs/LEDGER.md)

items.title: Scanner: count a $N as funded only when a label, the bounty bot or a maintainer posted it (contributor proposals dropped), read assignees and open linked PRs, rank by competition and file only free funded issues
items.why: The first board's top three could not be built (2026-10-11 build): tt-metal#59732 was assigned with a PR submitted, turso#8749's $650 was a contributor asking, SUSU-LABS#37 had two PRs open and omi's $250 rows were the issue authors' own proposals. Built 2026-10-11 (build): fundingOf/openPrs/takenBy in scripts/bounty-scanner.ts, Taken column on the board, 10 tests.
items.proof: the next board lists only funded issues with a Taken column and files only free ones

items.title: Claim ledger: a table in RESEARCH.md of every bounty attempted (issue, amount, PR, opened, merged, paid) kept by the build routine, and a weekly line in the report
items.why: The line's §4 numbers (claims, merges, payouts) have nowhere to live; without them the review cannot apply the kill rule. Built 2026-10-11 (burn-down): `## Claims` table in RESEARCH.md seeded with the three 10-11 reads, scripts/bounty-claims.ts (`npm run claims`, in `npm run check`) validates it and prints totals, kill-rule count and the week line; build, burn-down, weekly-report and review prompts updated; STRATEGY §4 row.
items.proof: the table exists and the weekly report reads it

items.title: Scanner: drop contests, showcases and usage tasks (an issue whose title or body pays for something other than a change to the repository) and file nothing under $25
items.why: Five of five scanner-filed items were dropped unbuilt by 2026-10-12: after the funding fix the next two were useagent#113 ("$5 per task" for recording oneself using the maintainer's product and emailing a report, AI runs banned) and Salam#1713 (a "build something with our language" reward paying the first two of twenty submissions). Neither is a fix on the repository and a day of work for $5 is not a line of income (STRATEGY §4 counts $50–$800 per merged PR). Built 2026-10-12 (burn-down): CONTEST_ISSUE on title + body in issueExcluded, MIN_AMOUNT = 25 in fileBounties (small ones stay on the board for the record), board header updated, 2 tests.
items.proof: the next board files no contest or sub-$25 item; the first filed item after this is a repository fix that a run can at least attempt

items.title: Bounty scanner: also drop issues whose result the claimant must record on a real device, claims the maintainer hands out first, and fixes that need hardware (the shapes bounty-scanner-contest-floor does not catch)
items.why: Built 2026-10-12 (build, the same slot as the burn-down's bounty-scanner-contest-floor, which this extends): the third filed item, useagent#61 ($80), passed the contest regex — it is a whole Expo app the maintainer assigns to one of four claimants and verifies on a real iPhone and Android with the claimant's own recordings; tt-metal#59732 (10-11) needed vendor hardware. SHAPE_RULES + shapeExcluded in scripts/bounty-scanner.ts, applied through issueExcluded after CONTEST_ISSUE on title and body; 2 tests on #61's real wording; board header and SCHEDULERS row say so.
items.proof: the next three boards file no item a read then drops for shape; first-bounty-pr unblocks on a real code item

items.title: Opire as a second bounty source: read docs.opire.dev/overview/commands and /rewards/pricing through the relay (the site is client-rendered; its landing page was read 2026-10-14), add OpireBot's funding comments and the Opire reward label to scripts/bounty-scanner.ts's funded-detection with a `not escrowed` note in the Taken column, and re-read the board once
items.why: Built 2026-10-14 (build): docs.opire.dev read through the relay (Docusaurus, pre-rendered) with Opire's app page and five GitHub searches. Only a code owner creates a bounty (`/reward N`, USD, from $20) and pays by hand after the merge; OpireBot's footer sits on every issue of a repository it is on (525 open since 07-16, three agent farms among them) and app-created rewards leave no GitHub trace, so the scanner strips the footer, reads a code owner's `/reward` and OpireBot's reward comment in the comments of footer issues, reads Opire's own open list from its server-rendered app page, marks the money `escrowed: false` (`free, not escrowed` under Taken; `(Opire, not escrowed)` in the filed title) and drops a `/reward` from anyone else as `reward not from a code owner`. Opire's whole open supply on 10-14: 6 rewards worth $212 on five issues, four from 2024–2025, none a free funded fix (RESEARCH.md). Original reason: Exchange 2026-W42: two boards under the new shape rules kept 0 free funded fixes, the Algora public board page (algora.io/bounties) now 404s and its docs host redirects to a recruiting site, so the Algora-labelled supply the line was validated on is thinner than the 10-11 count suggested. Opire's own page: bounties start at US$20, developers claim by pull request, and 'a claim does not create an automatic payment; the creator arranges payment only if the pull request meets the issue requirements' — weaker than an escrowed board, so the scanner must show it as such. A second source is the one lever left before the Sunday review applies a board-count kill trigger.
items.proof: the next board lists Opire-funded issues with their amounts and a `not escrowed` mark; the dropped-count table names the new rule

items.title: Bounty $30 (Opire, not escrowed) on trovu/trovu#329: Open target URLs not in PWA but in default browser — fork, fix with tests in the project's conventions, open the PR with `/claim #329` and a plain note on how it was built

Read CONTRIBUTING first; a project that forbids AI-assisted work is skipped and the item dropped. Dropped 2026-10-15 (build): the maintainer's 2026-05-23 body edit takes further PRs only with a video recorded on an Android phone showing the PWA opening Google in the system browser and the line "I am a human who is writing this comment, not an AI" — neither is something a routine can truthfully supply — and the 2026-06-17 edit says the feature may be technically impossible as PWAs stand; PR #718 was already open (the scanner's one-page timeline read missed it) and 60+ claimants since 2024 have had nothing merged; the 10-14 Opire read had already judged this issue not takeable. The scanner now pages the timeline and drops both shapes.
items.proof: PR merged and the bounty paid (revenue row in docs/LEDGER.md)

items.title: Bounty $30 on verdikta/verdikta-applications#76: [BOUNTY ~$30 x4] Post and fund a real task on Verdikta, publish a write-up (paid on Poidh, Base) — fork, fix with tests in the project's conventions, open the PR with `/claim #76` and a plain note on how it was built
items.why: Filed by the bounty scanner (2026-10-16, docs/bounties/BOARD.md): $30 posted on https://github.com/verdikta/verdikta-applications/issues/76 by a maintainer, the bounty bot or a label; free when filed (no assignee, no open PR); verdikta/verdikta-applications has 32 stars, JavaScript, MIT, 0 attempt comment(s). Read CONTRIBUTING first; a project that forbids AI-assisted work is skipped and the item dropped. Dropped 2026-10-16 (build): not a change to the repository — the claimant must post and fund an on-chain task from their own wallet (at least 0.0041 ETH, about $10, plus gas) on Base, get it completed by someone else, publish a 300-word write-up, and claim on Poidh with the funding transaction hash; the issue says "Nothing is paid for comments or pull requests on this issue". A £0 line spends nothing, crypto is out of scope (ARCHITECTURE), and the paying wallet is the owner's identity. The scanner now drops the shape (bounty-scanner-off-platform-pay).
items.proof: PR merged and the bounty paid (revenue row in docs/LEDGER.md)

items.title: Bounty scanner: also drop tasks the claimant must fund (post and fund, funded with at least N ETH, funding transaction hash) and slots paid to a wallet off GitHub (claim on Poidh not here, nothing is paid for pull requests)
items.why: Built 2026-10-16 (build): the eighth scanner-filed item in a row was dropped unbuilt — verdikta#76 ($30 x4) passed CONTEST_ISSUE and the three shape rules because it pays for posting and funding a task on-chain and claiming on Poidh, a shape no rule named. Fifth SHAPE_RULE in scripts/bounty-scanner.ts on #76's real wording, 6 assertions in the test, board header names the shape. The 10-16 board had 9 kept rows and this was its only free one; the next board shows whether anything free remains once the shape is gone.
items.proof: the next three boards file no item a read then drops for funding or off-GitHub payment

finished_reason: killed 2026-10-18 (review W42): seven consecutive daily boards 10-11..10-17 (about 3,900 issue reads) held 0 free funded code fixes at US$25+ and all 8 scanner-filed items were dropped on read — the review's kill rule for the line (STRATEGY §8 2026-10-11, §7 from today: a funded, free board row absent for a week). The labelled money on GitHub is assigned, crowded or not code; §3's recurring-job assumption failed on supply. Code, scanner and claims ledger kept; the exchange holds the idea parked with a re-open trigger (two consecutive weekly boards with a free, funded, escrowed code-with-tests row at US$25+).
